sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and client marker
sections.what: Marks the page to run in the browser and brings in the React helpers, the link component and the verification data type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs browser code to fetch data and update the screen.

sections.name: VerifierPage (part 1)
sections.title: Loading the verification record
sections.what: When the page opens, reads the anchor ID from the web address, asks the server for its verification, and tracks the loading and error state. A 404 gets a specific not-found message.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page needs fresh data each time the anchor changes.
sections.watch_out: The request uses the ID from the address, so renaming the route folder or the API path will break this page.

sections.name: VerifierPage (part 2)
sections.title: Error panel and result banners
sections.what: Shows an error panel with a return-home link when loading fails. When data arrives, shows a match or mismatch banner, then the case reference, signer and signed time.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes the result clear to people without technical knowledge.
sections.watch_out: If the signed time is not a valid date, the page will show an invalid date text.

sections.name: VerifierPage (part 3)
sections.title: Hash comparison and legal notice
sections.what: Shows the stored hash and the recomputed hash side by side with a match or mismatch tag, then a notice that the check shows no change since signing but does not prove ownership or legal title.
sections.why: Likely reason: the notice stops readers from treating the check as legal proof.
sections.watch_out: If the recomputed hash is missing, the page shows a message that the record was deleted or is missing, and it appears as a mismatch.

summary: A public web page that asks the server to check one anchor and shows whether the record still matches its stored fingerprint.
purpose: Lets anyone with an anchor ID see whether a record has changed since it was signed.
why: Likely reason: the check is public, so it needs no login. Other reasons are not stated in the code.
how: Reads the anchor ID from the web address, requests the verification from the server, shows a loading message, then either an error panel, or a match or mismatch banner with details, two hashes and a notice.
inputs: The anchor ID from the web address, and the verification record returned by the verify API.
outputs: The rendered verification page. The page saves nothing.
risks: The page shows every field the server returns, so any personal data the server sends would appear publicly. Only a 404 gets a specific message, and other failures get a generic one.
debug: Open the browser's network tab and find the verify request. A 404 means the anchor ID is not in the log. Check that the API route exists and returns the fields this page reads.
